title: The invitation is an interface
governingQuestion: When visibility is public but presence is permissioned, where does access actually live?
editorialHook: The URL is public. The room is not.
longformOutline: Map the official schedule as a layered permission system; open with the verified current surface, then expose the missing origin record.
verticalScriptBrief: Screen-record the public schedule path, stop at the boundary between information and entry, and end on G-ACCESS-01.
interactiveSpecification: Access Ledger: compare public listing, accreditation, invitation, venue entry, and retained data without collecting user information.
objectAndRightsBrief: Locate one historic invitation or schedule with item-level rights; leave the plate empty until G-OBJECT-04 closes.
teachingPrompt: Who can know an event exists, who can enter, and what evidence distinguishes those permissions?
communityCallout: Request dated LFW invitations, schedules, and accreditation instructions with provenance and contributor terms.
accessibilityPlan: Publish transcript/captions for time media; alt text or explicit designed-absence label; keyboard path for the interactive; no status conveyed by color alone.
releaseGates: Every positive claim resolves to cited support
Every media object has item-level rights disposition
Open gaps remain visible in copy and end cards
Named worker/interview consent recorded before quotation
mediaPolicy: OA/licensed/original/authorized embed only; selected documentary object installed with exact source-level treatment
status: evidence-backed production package; interviews and unresolved future reporting remain open

selectedObject.caption: The BFC records 50 digital-only, 21 hybrid and seven physical-only activations, making the permissions split explicit.
